question: Under profile enhanced and the KiCad plugin's default options, on the plugin's default board input (kicad_pcb), does `router.plane_obstacle_all_pours=true` (every signal-layer pour an obstacle for the nets with no pin or via inside it) lower KiCad's unconnected count after `--refill-zones`, summed over the registered boards, by more than the set's noise, with no routing-caused manufacturing breach or below-minimum copper in any arm, routing-caused DRC not up in total, no board worse by more than 2 unconnected and the route time at most 25 % more in total, so that it joins the ENHANCED table; and does the DSN path agree (secondary, reported)?
noise_why: routing-quality.md's totals rule for a change to profile enhanced: accept when the total improves by more than the set's noise, sqrt(sum of the per-board bands squared). canary-pwr's band is its registered 10 (docs/roadmap/prereg/K09.json `noise.canary-pwr`, N02's variant spread, as K14.json). No other board has a measured band, so each takes the rule's default max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), with `connections` the router's `board_statistics.connections.maximum_count` from the arm's result manifest (gate_totals.rs `default_band`; N06.15's source), the larger of the two arms as the gate takes it. The bands come from the inputs (the connection count of the board as loaded), not from the arms' results. Guard (3) uses the same bands per row (no row worse than its own band, decided 2026-10-21), which is stricter than the gate's own per-board clause ('no board worse than twice its band'), so guard (3) binds and is applied by hand from records.json and the gate's band lines

script.what: K13.5's version, unchanged (K13.json and K14.json pin the same hash): per router call ulimit -v ROUTE_MEMORY_KB and timeout -k 10 ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S; the plugin's own export or snapshot and import; grading as tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh --keep-tracks under the project's own .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru with the copper classes forced to error, `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --refill-zones` on the input and the routed board, routing-caused items on Q22.2's copper basis; SHARE_GRADE_WITH copies the grade of a byte-identical session

helper.what: new with this registration: `pours` (the eligibility rule), `prepare` (the boards), `run` (the commands) and `collect` (records.json for the gate and table.md with the secondary metrics); plain python3, no pcbnew (prepare calls kicad_steps.py strip through KICAD_PYTHON)

grading: per row, pcb-off then pcb-on, and on the rows of dsn_rows dsn-off then dsn-on; each -on arm with SHARE_GRADE_WITH its -off arm, so a session byte-identical to the baseline's copies its grade (summary grade_shared_with). Under the board's own rules (rules = project: the row's .kicad_pro and .kicad_dru, hashed in rules_files), the same oracle, metrics and manufacturing types as K13.6 and K14.6. kicad-cli only while `pgrep -x kicad-cli` shows none, one job at a time, no other heavy run at the same time
limits: every router call (the load check and the route) under ulimit -v 8000000 (ROUTE_MEMORY_KB) and timeout -k 10 300 (ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S); every route with `--max-passes 2 --timeout 240` after the plugin's flags (K15.4's and K15.13's runs: the pcu routes took 146.6-164.7 s and the canary-pwr routes 49.1-149.7 s at these flags; the demos and corpus boards are smaller). A call that hits ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S or is killed by a signal (exit status 124 or above) is aborted = 1 and not graded. A route the router's own --timeout stopped (result manifest final_state TIMED_OUT) depends on the machine's speed, so its row is not judged (validity (b)). Estimated time: 38 calls; the pcu and canary-pwr calls about 20 min together (K15.13: routes 49-165 s, plus 5-15 s of snapshot or export, load and KiCad DRC per call), the 30 other calls (15 smaller boards) about 15-30 min, so about 35-50 min in all; the bound if every call hit ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S is 38 x about 330 s = 3.5 h

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: summary via_in_pad: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board minus the input board's, floored at 0 (D8)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: summary below_minimum: routed tracks and vias (whose nanometre copper key the input board does not have) under the Board Setup minimum track width, via diameter or via drill, summed
metric_definitions.manufacturing_breaches: summary manufacturing_breaches: the routing-caused KiCad DRC items (Q22.2's copper basis) of the types clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items, summed
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: the signal: summary unconnected, kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the routed board after --refill-zones
metric_definitions.zone_zone_unconnected: secondary: the routed board's unconnected items (routed/drc.json, or the shared grade's) whose items are all zones: a pour split into islands that KiCad cannot join (K15.13's count)
metric_definitions.zone_zone_zones: the distinct (net, layer) zones those items name
metric_definitions.router_incomplete: the router's own incomplete connections at the end: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.incomplete_count (work/<name>.result.json)
metric_definitions.kicad_less_router: secondary: kicad_unconnected - router_incomplete, how far KiCad's count is above the router's (K15.13: 31 and 43 off, 3 and 5 on, on pcu)
metric_definitions.drc_real: guard (2): the sum of summary routing_caused_by_type (the grader's drc_real), every type
metric_definitions.route_seconds: guard (4): summary route_s, the routing call's wall-clock seconds
metric_definitions.connections: the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.maximum_count: the board's connections as the router loaded it, the default noise band's base
metric_definitions.input_unconnected: summary input_unconnected: kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the stripped input board
metric_definitions.pour_guard_pours: N of the route log's 'Pour guard: N pour(s) of every net class ...' line, 0 when there is none (validity (a))

validity: checked before keep_rule, per row: (a) the setting reached the router: each -on arm's route.log has the line 'Pour guard: N pour(s) of every net class block the nets with no pin or via inside them (M exemptions).' and no -off arm has it; a row whose -on arm lists N = 0 pours is judged as it is (the setting does nothing there) and named; (b) the row is judged when every arm it runs has aborted 0, graded true and final_state COMPLETED; (c) amendment 1 is written before the first arm and `cargo test -p freerouting-dev --test prereg_k15_14` passes in TREE. A row that fails (a) or (b), or whose board is missing, is left out of the judgement and reported by name with its reason (decided 2026-10-21); the keep rule, guards (2)-(4) and the set noise are then over the judged rows only. The measurement is 'not measured' (decision_table) only when fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows are judged, pcu-76163c7 is not judged, or (c) fails
guards: (1) in every arm that runs and is graded, judged row or not: manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0, absolutely (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's manufacturing rules; routing-quality.md, order of importance items 1 and 2); the gate's HARD lines of the verdict pair, the reported pair and the two DSN invocations, and summary.json for the rows left out. (2) routing-caused DRC not up: the sum of drc_real over the judged rows in pcb-on is at most pcb-off's. (3) no row worse than its own noise band (decided 2026-10-21): on every judged row, pcb-on's kicad_unconnected is at most pcb-off's + the row's band, the totals rule's per-row band (canary-pwr-95882f00 10, every other row max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), noise_why). (4) route time: the sum of route_seconds over the judged rows in pcb-on is at most 1.25 x pcb-off's. Guards (2)-(4) are on the primary input; on the DSN arms they are reported
keep_rule: kept when validity holds (at least 3 distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 among them, (c)), guard (1) holds, the signal improves (S: the sum of pcb-on's kicad_unconnected over the judged rows is lower than pcb-off's by more than the set noise sqrt(sum of the bands squared), noise_why; strictly more, as the gate computes it) and guards (2), (3) and (4) hold. The DSN arms (dsn_rows only) decide nothing beyond guard (1); their totals, Zone-Zone items and kicad_less_router are reported
keep_rule_by_hand: from OUT/records.json and OUT/table.md (`python3 -I TREE/tools/bench/k15_all_pours.py collect docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.14.json OUT`) and the gate (TREE's freerouting-dev, the commands of heavy_run's last step): `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --write-baseline`, then `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --all-pairs [--rows <the judged rows>]`, then `gate ... --arms dsn-off,dsn-on --rows pcu-76163c7,canary-pwr-95882f00` and `gate ... --arms dsn-on,dsn-off --rows pcu-76163c7,canary-pwr-95882f00` (DSN, reported; their 'N=2' refusal of the three-board minimum is expected). The verdict pair's 'totals verdict' line is S, with the set noise it prints; its HARD lines and the reported pairs' are guard (1); guards (2)-(4) are summed by hand from records.json; validity (a) and (b) from the route logs and table.md's state column. The reverse pair and the dsn-on,dsn-off invocation are there for their HARD lines only; their totals verdicts are the verdict pair's mirror and are not read. collect writes each row's `connections` (the largest of its arms') for the gate's default band; the format was checked on K15.13's existing pcu and canary-pwr outputs before registration (0 refusals; no new number). With a row left out (validity), --all-pairs runs with --rows naming the judged rows, and that output is the verdict

decision_table.not measured: fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 not judged, or validity (c) fails (a row left out by validity (a) or (b) does not by itself make the measurement 'not measured': it is reported by name and the other rows are judged): K15.14 stays [~] naming the rows and reasons; nothing changes in the product; the rows are run again only after the cause is fixed (a longer timeout_s or a fix), under an amendment naming it, with nothing else changed
decision_table.breach: the measurement is not 'not measured' and guard (1) fails in any graded arm (of a judged row or not): K15.14 stays [~] naming the arm, row and items; the breach is fixed in an item of its own (a pcb-on or dsn-on breach that the -off arm lacks is a defect of the setting; one in an -off arm is a defect of today's default), then the registered run repeats at the fixed commit under an amendment; until then the setting stays opt-in and the plugin does not offer it (decided 2026-10-20: fix gains, don't remove them; never ship below-minimum copper)
decision_table.not kept, no gain: neither of the above, and S fails over the judged rows: the setting stays opt-in, unset in both profiles; the plugin offers it as an option (options.py field and to_args flag, the dialog's checkbox, a plugin test), K15.14's note records the table; DIVERGENCES' K15.13 entry gets the numbers
decision_table.not kept, guard: none of the above, S holds and any of guards (2), (3), (4) fails over the judged rows: the setting stays opt-in and the plugin offers it as an option (as 'not kept, no gain'); K15.14's note names the failing guard and its rows, and a follow-up item may fix the cost and measure again under a new registration (fix gains, don't remove them)
decision_table.kept: none of the above: validity, guard (1), S and guards (2), (3), (4) all hold over the judged rows: `router.plane_obstacle_all_pours` joins the ENHANCED table (crates/freerouting/src/settings/profile.rs) as true; a test pins enhanced's value and legacy's unset (tests/settings_defaults.rs or the profile tests); DIVERGENCES' enhanced section gets the line with this measurement's totals; `legacy` unchanged: `PARITY_SET=tools/bench/sets/connection-parity.txt tools/parity-check.sh --no-probes` 7 of 7 exact; the plugin passes nothing new (the profile carries it)
decision_table.order: the rows are tried in the order not measured, breach, not kept no gain, not kept guard, kept; the first whose condition holds decides, so every outcome maps to exactly one row

known_effects: both inputs give each pour the same model (K15.13's Found: a conduction area that is no obstacle, connected to every pin and via centred in its outline), so with the setting off a crossing trace costs the router nothing and KiCad's refill splits the pour. With it on, foreign nets with no pin or via inside a pour route around it, which costs room: on canary-pwr K15.13 saw the router's incomplete rise (27 -> 38 on kicad_pcb) while KiCad's count fell (40 -> 36). Nets exempt under Q01's rule (a pin inside the outline) still cross and can still split a pour (K15.13's V_INRUSH, D11_C, BAT_FETS). The pcu board's V_BUS_12V via_dangling items (K15.15, overlapping plane-layer zones) were in both arms of K15.13 (3 on the kicad_pcb path), so they largely cancel in guard (2). Both arms import the session whole, as the plugin does (fix_existing off), on stripped boards with no input copper
